data.description:
# AGENTS.md tells agents to override `default_assignee` with a bare handle, which reconcile then clears

## Context / Problem

`AGENTS.md` — the canonical, launch-loaded agent guidance — instructs agents to claim with an
explicit assignee in **three** places:

- `AGENTS.md:75` — "`claim <id> --assignee <you>` … as the FIRST step of working a ticket"
- `AGENTS.md:106` — "**Grab work atomically** — `claim <id> --assignee <you>`"
- `AGENTS.md:238` (library quick reference) — `rebar.claim(tid["id"], assignee="me")`

Two problems compound:

1. **It instructs an override of a setting that exists precisely to get this right.**
   `rebar.toml:66` configures `default_assignee = "joeoakhart@navapbc.com"`, and
   `_commands/claim.py:124-125` applies it **only** when `--assignee` is omitted
   (`if assignee is None`). Because `AGENTS.md` says to always pass `--assignee`, the
   configured default is **never** reached on the agent path.
2. **"`<you>`" / `assignee="me"` invite a bare handle.** An agent substitutes its own
   identity — e.g. `RebarBotNava`, or literally `me` as the library example shows — and
   `AGENTS.md` gives no hint that the value must be Jira-resolvable.

The consequence is a silent revert. The reconciler cannot resolve a bare handle to a Jira
user, treats the ticket as unassigned, and the inbound differ writes `assignee=""` back over
the local value. Work ends up attributed to nobody.

`docs/config.md:397-400` already documents the requirement correctly — "Use a **Jira-resolvable
identity** (email or accountId) … a bare, ambiguous handle (e.g. `joe`) is left unassigned
rather than mis-assigned (bug 544e)" — so the two documents **contradict each other**, and the
one agents actually read at launch is the wrong one. `AGENTS.md` never mentions
`default_assignee` at all.

This is the documented failure mode of closed bug `544e-0a25-eabb-4220`, and story
`c36c-357a-2900-4ed7` added `default_assignee` specifically to fix it — but `AGENTS.md` was
never updated to stop overriding it, so the fix does not reach agents.

## Evidence (observed live, epic e369)

Claimed the epic and story J1 with `--assignee RebarBotNava`, following `AGENTS.md`. Both
reported success (`CLAIMED: acb2-… (assignee: RebarBotNava)`) and both later read back
`assignee = ''`.

The event log proves the store write was correct and that no event ever wrote the empty string:

```
ticket: CLAIM acb2-1823-2f0d-415b
  EDIT.json -> "data":{"fields":{"assignee":"RebarBotNava"}}
```

Every subsequent assignee-bearing EDIT also wrote `"RebarBotNava"`. The `''` therefore comes
from a later reconciler-authored EDIT, exactly as session log `bb27-06bf-b868-42c7` recorded
with a live reproduction:

> "Event log for 3d3d: claim wrote EDIT {assignee:\"joe\"}; ~143s later a reconciler-authored
> EDIT wrote {assignee:\"\"} — the clobber. Live API: validate_assignee_exists(\"joe\")
> REJECTED (\"3 Joes, ambiguous\"); \"joeoakhart@navapbc.com\" RESOLVED to accountId
> 712020:6471376f-…"

Control: throwaway probe tickets (not Jira-bound) **retained** `RebarBotNava` indefinitely,
confirming the clear is reconcile-side and not a `claim` parsing or persistence defect.

Note `claimed_session` and `claim_harness` survive the clobber, so the claim is still
attributable — but `assignee`, which `list`/`ready`/`next-batch` and every human reader use,
is not.

## Approach

Fix the guidance, not the code — `claim`'s explicit-wins precedence is correct and
`default_assignee` already works.

1. **`AGENTS.md`** — change the claim instruction to omit `--assignee` so the configured
   default applies: `claim <id>` (noting it auto-assigns `ticket.default_assignee`). Where an
   explicit assignee is genuinely needed, state that it MUST be a Jira-resolvable identity
   (email/accountId), never a bare handle, with a one-line pointer to
   `docs/config.md#ticketdefault_assignee`. Update all three sites (`:75`, `:106`, `:238` —
   the library example `assignee="me"` is the worst offender).
2. Consider a **warning at claim time** when an explicit assignee is a bare handle (no `@`,
   not an accountId shape) while a `default_assignee` is configured — turning a silent
   revert into a visible nudge. Optional; the doc fix is the blocking part.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md`'s claim guidance no longer instructs an unconditional `--assignee` override; it
      shows `claim <id>` and states that `ticket.default_assignee` is applied automatically
- [ ] all three sites (`AGENTS.md:75`, `:106`, and the `:238` library example) are updated
      consistently, and `assignee="me"` no longer appears as a recommended value
- [ ] where an explicit assignee is documented, `AGENTS.md` states it must be Jira-resolvable
      (email/accountId) and links to `docs/config.md#ticketdefault_assignee`
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` and `docs/config.md` no longer contradict each other on assignee identity
- [ ] a fresh agent following ONLY `AGENTS.md` produces a ticket whose assignee survives a
      reconcile pass (verifiable by claiming a scratch ticket and confirming the assignee is
      non-empty after one bridge cycle)
data.title: AGENTS.md tells agents to override default_assignee with a bare handle, which reconcile clears
